code.description:
The stable name of the failure. Branch on this, not on `error`.

- `INVALID_BODY` — The body did not parse, or a field is out of range.
- `INVALID_QUERY` — A query parameter names something impossible.
- `BODY_TOO_LARGE` — The request body is over the route’s ceiling.
- `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` — The bytes are not a format this route can read.
- `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` — The path exists, but not with this method. See the Allow header.
- `CLIENT_TOO_OLD` — This build of the client is older than the floor this server answers. `minimum` says which build to update to.
- `UNAUTHENTICATED` — No session, or one that has expired.
- `FORBIDDEN` — A session, but not the capability this route needs.
- `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` — The account exists but has been switched off.
- `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` — The e-mail and password do not match an account.
- `TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS` — Too many failed sign-ins from this address, or against this e-mail. See Retry-After.
- `NOT_FOUND` — No such record, or none this account may see.
- `ITEM_NOT_FOUND` — No such item card.
- `CASE_NOT_FOUND` — No such case.
- `ORGANIZER_NOT_FOUND` — No such organizer.
- `BRAND_NOT_FOUND` — No such maker.
- `USER_NOT_FOUND` — No such account.
- `ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND` — No such address.
- `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` — No such session, or none belonging to this account.
- `PHOTO_NOT_FOUND` — No such photograph, or its file is gone.
- `MANUAL_NOT_FOUND` — No such document, or its file is gone.
- `LABEL_NOT_FOUND` — No such label, or its file is gone.
- `SEARCH_ENGINE_NOT_FOUND` — No search engine or cutout method by that name.
- `LABEL_SLOT_NOT_FOUND` — This case has no such label slot.
- `ITEM_NOT_IN_ORGANIZER` — That item is not in this organizer.
- `EMAIL_TAKEN` — An account with that e-mail already exists.
- `ADDRESS_NAME_TAKEN` — Another place is already called that.
- `SERIAL_NUMBER_TAKEN` — Another card already carries that serial number.
- `ATTRIBUTE_NAME_TAKEN` — This card already has a parameter with that name.
- `BRAND_NAME_TAKEN` — A maker with that name already exists.
- `LOGO_TAKEN` — That picture is already another maker’s logo.
- `LABEL_SLOT_TAKEN` — This case already has a slot that size.
- `ORGANIZER_NUMBER_TAKEN` — Another organizer already has that number.
- `ITEM_IS_NOT_A_TOOL` — Only tools go in an organizer. This card is an appliance or a case.
- `ITEM_IS_NOT_A_CASE` — Only a case has places for labels. This card is a tool or an appliance.
- `ITEM_IN_ORGANIZER` — This card is in an organizer, so it cannot stop being a tool until it is taken out.
- `ITEM_ALREADY_IN_ORGANIZER` — That item is in another organizer already.
- `PHOTO_ALREADY_ON_CARD` — That photograph is already on this card.
- `MANUAL_ALREADY_ON_CARD` — That document is already on this card.
- `LAST_ACTIVE_ADMIN` — The change would leave the installation with no admin.
- `SELF_ROLE_CHANGE` — An account cannot change or delete itself here.
- `PAGE_UNREACHABLE` — The product page would not load.
- `NOT_A_PRODUCT_PAGE` — There is no product card at that address.
- `UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE` — No importer can read that host.
- `NO_SOURCE_PAGE` — This card was not imported, so there is no page to read.
- `SOURCE_HAS_NO_MANUALS` — That source publishes no documents.
- `DOWNLOAD_FAILED` — Every address in the request failed to download.
- `IMAGE_UNREADABLE` — The bytes are not an image this server can decode.
- `NOT_A_PDF` — The bytes are not a PDF.
- `CUTOUT_UNSUITABLE` — The picture is not one this method can cut out.
- `CUTOUT_UNAVAILABLE` — No cutout method is configured and enabled.
- `PREVIEW_EXPIRED` — The preview has been swept, or is damaged.
- `LABEL_UNDRAWABLE` — The label cannot be drawn from what the catalog says now.
- `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE` — No search engine is configured and enabled.
- `ATTACH_FAILED` — None of the selected records could be attached.
- `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` — Postgres is unreachable. The request was fine; retry.
- `INTERNAL` — Something went wrong that the caller cannot act on.

info.description:
The HTTP contract of the ToolTrack catalog: one card per physical item,
searchable from a phone on site, with three roles deciding who may look
and who may change things.

Every route but the handful tagged `public` needs the session cookie that
`POST /api/auth/login` sets. Prose in a response — including the `error`
field — follows the `Accept-Language` header, so it is never something to
branch on; the status code is.

Only `name` is required, and it is the part a picker shows — a crew says "magazyn", not a postcode. Names are unique folded and trimmed, so "Magazyn" and "magazyn " are one place rather than two lines nobody can choose between.

post.description:
The same door as `login`, for a client with no cookie jar worth relying on. It answers with the token itself and sets no cookie; send it back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which wins over a cookie when both are present.

Two doors, one session: the same row, the same expiry, the same revocation. `login` deliberately does not answer with a token — a token in a response body is one any script on the page can read, and that is what the httpOnly cookie exists to prevent.

`device` is a label for the session list and nothing else. It is never read while authenticating.

The same throttle as `login`, counting against the same totals: a limit guarding one of two doors into the same house is one a caller walks around.

get.description:
The chosen labels ganged onto A4, as a PDF to look at and print.

A **GET** because the screen opens it in a tab, and a tab is a GET — which is also why the ids arrive in the query string rather than in a body. Nothing is stored: the sheet is a view of labels that already exist.

The artwork is drawn again with no margin or crop marks rather than taken from each label’s own file — thirty margins is most of a sheet of paper — which also means a sheet can never show something a label no longer says. That redrawing is why there is a ceiling of 200: each one takes a moment, and a full sheet is tens of seconds of a single request.

A label whose photographs have gone missing does not cost the other twenty-nine their sheet. What could not be drawn is printed **on the sheet itself**, because the answer here is a file in a new tab and nothing reads a header or a status line — a sheet of a hundred and ninety-four would otherwise be indistinguishable from the two hundred that were asked for.
